note: P-256 point arithmetic needs no signature, so the fixture's ACTUAL compiled locking script runs on @bsv/sdk's Spend engine with concrete points. Every expected point is OpenSSL's (crypto.createECDH('prime256v1') with the scalar as private key), NOT compiler output. The k=2 and P+P spends are the two defects fixed here: p256Mul(G,2n) returned 64 zero bytes and p256Add(G,G) returned a wrong point.

spends.note: p256Mul(G, 2) == 2G — the scalar that returned the all-zero point
p256MulGen(2) == 2G — same ladder, generator entry point
p256Add(G, G) == 2G — the affine doubling case that returned a wrong point
p256Mul(G, 3) == 3G != the committed 2G — proves the accepts are not vacuous
